  `msm_id` bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `user_id` bigint DEFAULT NULL,
  `filter_id` bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `offer_id` bigint NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `reward` varchar(1000) DEFAULT 'na',
  `reward_expiry` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `unicode_message` enum('on', 'off') NOT NULL DEFAULT 'off',
  `customers_dnd_fail` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `customers_invalidphone_fail` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `customers_network_fail` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `customers_coupon_fail` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '0',
  `customers_dlt_template_fail` int DEFAULT '0',
  `customers_fill_incomplete` int DEFAULT '0',

  `batches_suppressed` int DEFAULT NULL,

  `run_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `is_image` int DEFAULT NULL,
  `image_url` varchar(500) DEFAULT NULL,
  `abenabled` int DEFAULT '0',
  `abpercentage` int DEFAULT '0',
  `trackdays` int NOT NULL DEFAULT '7',
  `approved_by` bigint DEFAULT NULL,
  `approval_time` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `cta_url` varchar(500) DEFAULT NULL,
  `notification_status` longtext,
  `error_id` bigint DEFAULT NULL,
  `vendor_id` mediumtext,

) ENGINE = InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET = latin1```
It's unclear from logs which column to look for invalid UTF-8, also if data is available in MySQL then it should be replicated either by sanitising UTF-8

Hi <@U0A5EGHRLQY> thanks for flagging this. We've identified the root cause, the source table has a BLOB column `name: blob`, and our MySQL connector currently treats BLOB column as plain text instead of raw binary data. Since these columns can contain bytes that aren't valid UTF-8 text, the sync fails when writing to Iceberg.

We already have a fix in progress <https://github.com/datazip-inc/olake/pull/1183|(PR #1183)> that adds proper binary type support end-to-end . We'll share an ETA shortly. Thanks!
